name: Read, follow and search an app's logs
covers: The App logs tab for an app with an nlog.config: the live log growing as the service writes, a search highlighting matches, a regular expression, and Search all marking the zipped archive that has them

steps.note: An nlog.config, as an app that logs with NLog has, pointing at the heartbeat log the service writes, and two older logs in the archive folder it names, one of them zipped as NLog zips them.
powershell: '2026-10-19 09:00:10 1.0.0 region West | ORD-1042 payment declined again')

steps.say: main now has an nlog.config, as an app that logs with NLog would. It says the log is logs\heartbeat.log, the file the service writes its heartbeat to, with older logs in logs\archive, one of them zipped.
Open the App logs tab, which shows because main has an nlog.config

steps.what: the live log in the list of logs

steps.say: The live log is open. The service writes a line every 30 seconds, as main's settings say, and it shows here as it is written.

steps.what: the log's text, for a new heartbeat line

steps.say: Search the live log for region
Each match is highlighted in yellow, the one in view in orange: ${first}. The arrows go to the next and the one before.
Search for ORD-10 and a number, as a regular expression

steps.what: No matches in the live log

steps.say: Click Search all, to search every log, the zipped one too

steps.what: the search of every log finishing
the zipped log, marked with 2 matches
steps.say: Open the zipped log that has the matches

steps.checkpoint: The app's logs could be read, followed and searched

checks.label: The live log showed the service's heartbeat
Searching the live log found region
ORD-10 and a number wasn't in the live log
Search all found it in 1 of the 3 logs
The plain archive was marked as having no matches
The zipped log opened from inside its zip

look: A new heartbeat line showed without doing anything.
The list on the left has LIVE, with heartbeat.log, then ARCHIVED, with heartbeat.1.log and heartbeat.2.log in heartbeat.2.zip.
heartbeat.2.log has a yellow 2 beside it, and heartbeat.1.log and heartbeat.log are faded.
Both ORD-1042 in the zipped log are highlighted, the first in orange, and the box above it says 1 of 2.
Lines are coloured by their level when a log has one, such as ERROR in red.
